newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar U.S. dealer inventories up.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar U.S. dealer inventories up.

text.p: Caterpillar Inc said Tuesday U.S. dealers' new machine inventories increased in 1996 from 1995 due to improved economic and industry outlooks.
At the end of the year, U.S. inventories were moderately above normal relative to current selling rates, the heavy equipment maker said.
Outside the United States, inventories declined and at year-end were about normal relative to current selling rates, Caterpillar said.
Sales inside the United States in 1996 were $7.67 billion, up from $7.42 billion a year ago. Sales outside the United States were $8.14 billion, up from $8.03 billion a year ago, the company said.
Earlier Tuesday, the company reported net income of $381 million, or $1.99 a share in the fourth quarter, up from $300 million, or $1.53 a share a year ago.

The company said price realization improved in the quarter from a year ago, but added that part of the improvement was due to the absence of currency hedges in 1996 that had about a $30 million adverse impact on fourth-quarter prices.
Caterpillar shares were down 1-1/4 at 77-1/4 Tuesday.
